source: SCG Chemicals HAZOP - LOPA Guideline SD-PS-G-0209 (Appendix B Tables B1/B2, Appendix G risk matrix)

risk_matrix.note: rows = frequency category F-1..F-5, columns = consequence category C-1..C-5, value = risk rank 1..4 (I..IV)

frequency_categories.label: Likely to occur at least once in the lifetime of the process
Unlikely to occur in the lifetime of the process, but possible
Extremely unlikely - not realistically expected to occur

consequence_categories.safety: Fatal injury or irreversible health effects

risk_ranks.label: I
risk_ranks.name: Intolerable
risk_ranks.action: Develop recommendations to reduce risk to category III

risk_ranks.label: II
risk_ranks.name: Undesirable
risk_ranks.action: Develop recommendations to reduce risk to category III

risk_ranks.label: III
risk_ranks.name: Tolerable with controls
risk_ranks.action: Team may make recommendations to reduce risk

initiating_events.label: Unloading/loading hose failure (annual inspection and replacement)
Turbine/diesel engine over speed with casing breach
Pumps and other rotating equipment failure
Fixed equipment failure (e.g. exchanger tube failure)
Single check valve failure on high demand mode
Double check valves in series failure (dissimilar) on high demand mode
Operator failure, routine task once per week or more often
Operator failure, routine task between once per month and once per week
Operator failure, non-routine task less than once per month
LOTO procedure failure while following a written checklist (per opportunity)
Not a credible HAZOP initiating event (natural event, external impact, double jeopardy, incredible manual valve error, single point of failure)

ipl_types.label: Open vent (no valve)
End-of-line deflagration flame arrester
In-line deflagration / detonation arrester
Overflow line to safe location, no impediment to flow
Overflow line with passive fluid or rupture disk
Overflow line that could freeze, foul or be valved closed
Permanent mechanical stop that limits travel (e.g. valve clamp)
Inherently safe design (e.g. design pressure exceeds all challenges)
Continuous pilot
Captive key / lock system (e.g. Ellis key lock)
Adjustable movement-limiting device (car seal, chain/lock)
Restriction orifice (clean, non-corrosive service)
Multiple mechanical pump seal with failure detection
Human response to alarm / routine check / verification check
BPCS control loop or interlock (not IEC 61511, max 1 credit)
Safety instrumented function SIL 1
Safety instrumented function SIL 2
Safety instrumented function SIL 3
Relief valve designed for the scenario
Relief valve / rupture disc with block valve and no CSO management system
Rupture disc designed for the scenario
Breather / pressure-vacuum valve
Emergency vent hatch (credited like a relief device, as in the engineer worksheet)
Single check valve, low-demand mode (not sole IPL for reverse-flow overpressure)
Double check valves of dissimilar type, low-demand mode
Second pressure regulator as IPL
